key_insight: Predicting a good simplex warm start is not enough—measured solver cost depends strongly on how the start is chosen, not just on how many iterations it saves.
engineering_relevance: For practical LP solvers, CostStart can cut end-to-end solve time much more reliably than basis prediction alone by optimizing for actual CPU work.
method: Train a supervised model to predict which variables should be basic at optimality.
Measure solver instruction counts and train a small policy to choose warm-start size, algorithm, pricing rule, or no warm start.
Select the start that minimizes measured cost rather than relying only on basis overlap or pivot count.
evidence_signal: Across 25 LP classes, the method removed about two thirds of dual-simplex iterations but only about one third of runtime; on unseen test LPs it roughly halved solve time and outperformed prior retrained methods by 1.4–2.2×.
watch_item: Instruction-count-based tuning may depend on solver implementation details and hardware, so gains may not transfer unchanged across different LP solvers or compute environments.
paper_title: Learning Warm Starts for the Simplex Method from Measured Solver Cost
